title: DOE-EM seeks proposals for Hanford site development projects
summary: The Department of Energy’s Office of Environmental Management has announced that it is accepting proposals for industrial development of portions of the Hanford Reservation near Richland, Wash. According to a November 6 press release, as part of its American Energy Hubs initiative, DOE-EM seeks to lease plots of land to companies pursuing projects in “affordable energy generation, advanced manufacturing, critical materials development, and computing capabilities.” The request for offer requires project developers to “build, bring, or buy” the energy required for the project’s operations, though the power generation facility does not need to be co-located on site. Developers working on energy generation or storage initiatives will be responsible for establishing connections with electric utilities.

title: UK Nuclear Professionals Confident, But Warn Of Uncertainties And Challenges
summary: Nuclear professionals are confident about the future of the UK industry, but warn that funding uncertainty, skills shortages and challenges delivering major projects could hamper its growth, according to new research from the Nuclear Institute. A survey of Nuclear Institute members found that almost four in five (79.7%) respondents are optimistic about the industry’s future, with a third of these (33.3%) describing themselves as very optimistic. However, the research also highlighted concerns over the industry’s ability to turn ambition into action, with respondents identifying project costs, workforce capacity, regulatory barriers and long-term government support among its most pressing challenges.

title: CoP webinar explores reactor developer’s perspective on RIPB regulation
summary: The American Nuclear Society’s Risk-informed, Performance-based Principles and Policy Committee (RP3C) recently held another presentation in its monthly Community of Practice (CoP) series, the RP3C’s final CoP of the year. Former RP3C chair N. Prasad Kadambi opened the meeting with brief introductory remarks about the RP3C and the value of risk-informed, performance-based (RIPB) techniques as opposed to conventional prescriptive and deterministic approaches.

title: Estonia Shortlists Three Locations For First BWRX-300 Nuclear Power Plant
summary: Estonia said it will now focus on three potential locations in the Viru-Nigula region in the north of the country for the development of its first nuclear power plants having discarded three sites for what it called “national security reasons”. In a statement, the Estonian government said that the Madala, Malla and Letipea sites would be the three sites considered to host Estonia-based project development company Fermi Energia’s planned development of two 300-MW GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy BWRX-300 small modular reactors (SMRs). Three sites in Lüganuse municipality, also in the north of the country, were excluded from plans due to national defence reasons, a decision based on assessment guidelines outlined by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) for the risk profile of sites.

title: China Pours First Concrete For HTGR At ‘World’s First’ Hybrid Nuclear Power Station
summary: The first batch of concrete has been poured for the nuclear island of the high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) that forms part the first phase of a hybrid nuclear power station in Jiangsu province, eastern China. The facility, known as the Jiangsu Xuwei Nuclear Heating and Power Plant, will supply both industrial heat and electricity by coupling the Chilong One HTGR with two Hualong One pressurised water reactors (PWRs). CNNC said first concrete had now been poured for the 600-MW HTGR. That follows the pouring of first concrete in January for the nuclear island of Unit 1, a Hualong One PWR.
